memory_update.text: AMKR should remain in the Layer 1B universe as a US-listed OSAT and direct packaging/test capacity candidate, but survival depends on evidence that advanced packaging utilization and customer programs are material.
FORM is a high-quality underfollowed testing-gate candidate because HBM and 2.5D/3D packaging increase known-good-die and probe-card complexity.
KLIC is a mid-cap equipment candidate with advanced packaging/TCB optionality; classify as inference until HBM production qualification and customer-specific demand are better verified.
ONTO is a process-control and metrology candidate for the HBM/advanced packaging yield layer; monitor whether HBM-related purchase agreements convert into durable backlog and revenue.

Further Layer 1C work should search non-US ADRs and Taiwan-listed OSAT/memory-backend specialists such as Powertech, KYEC, ASE, and substrate suppliers, because the highest-purity capacity beneficiaries may not be US common stocks.

node: Advanced packaging, HBM backend, OSAT, and memory package/test capacity
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe for the underfollowed lane around HBM backend, advanced packaging, OSAT, and memory/package-test capacity. The strongest direct candidates are not the HBM producers themselves but package/test capacity owners and yield-enabling equipment or test vendors: Amkor for OSAT capacity, FormFactor for HBM/known-good-die wafer probe, Kulicke & Soffa for thermocompression bonding equipment, and Onto Innovation for inspection/metrology tied to advanced packaging and HBM expansion. These are research candidates only, not buy/sell recommendations.
